summary: The article argues that volunteer coaches in amateur sports are essential yet underappreciated, giving examples of four coaches who devote time, money and mentorship to community teams. It describes the financial strain and risk of burnout they face, and calls on administrative bodies, local governments and the wider community to offer recognition, training and resources.
one_line: Volunteer coaches in amateur sports give huge unpaid time, money and mentorship but are undervalued, and communities and officials should recognize and support them.
key_facts: As of October 17, 2023, the article says local sports thrive on the work of volunteer coaches who rarely get due recognition.
James Carter is an accountant by day and a volunteer basketball coach at Briggs Community Center since September 2023.
Carter, like many coaches, spends nearly 20 hours a week on plays, practices and mentoring without financial compensation.
Maria Gonzalez has led the local soccer team since September 5, 2023, and attends every practice, game and fundraising event.
Michael Johnson started coaching little league baseball in early September 2023 and found he was also teaching kids to handle failure, work as a team and show sportsmanship.
Emma Thompson took charge of a local swim team on the brink of shutdown in late September 2023.
Coaches like Thompson often use their own money or spend countless hours fundraising to keep teams afloat.
Underappreciation can be demoralizing and may lead to burnout, causing amateur sports to lose mentors and advocates.
Administrative bodies and local governments are often lacking in support; the article says support need not mean stipends but acknowledgment, training and resources.
Coaches need access to skill-upgrading courses, sports equipment and help with administrative tasks.
Suggested community recognition includes verbal acknowledgement, community awards, features in local newspapers and celebration at seasonal sports events or gatherings.
The article concludes that volunteer coaches are 'shaping the very fabric of our society' and their role cannot be underestimated.
